chapter.title: Chapter Two: Red Side Tapes
chapter.subtitle: Everybody kept something. Nobody kept quiet enough.
chapter.description: A private recording blows up the family while you fight through the Red Side Gauntlet.

tips: Follow the conversation at your own pace.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Snitch, out.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: I'm *not* filming—

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: Both phones, Snitch. *(She points without looking.)*We can see the light through your pocket. We're not going to do the thing where you turn it off slowly, we're going to do the thing where you

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: put it on the table face down, and *then* you're going to turn around so we can all watch you do it.

scenes.speaker: Snitch
scenes.text: *(He does it. He turns around after.)* *(Beat.)* You know, in *eight years* of media work, that's the first time anybody's ever asked me to *turn around*.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Turn around *often*.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Before I press anything. It was three weeks after the memorial. That's — that's the honest number, that's when he sent it, that's when it *arrived*. He didn't call. He sent a *thing* through me.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Three weeks.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Three weeks.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Very flat.)* Go on.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *[tape — Red's voice, older, in a different room]*

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *[tape]* Red, it's me. You said the baby came. Tell her I know. Tell her I'm alive. I'll call when I can.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Not immediately. She waits until the machine clicks off.)* He didn't call.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: He didn't call.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: He said he would call.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: He didn't.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Three weeks after my husband is dead. Three weeks after I stood up in that church. *(Beat.)*And at the time this was made, I was three weeks pregnant with a man who was *not dead*, who was

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *somewhere*, having a *conversation* with a *recorder*.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Baby Momma—

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Don't. I'm not finished. I have been *finished* for four years, I have been finished in *every room* I have walked into since the second of March, and I am *not finished* right now, so you're

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: going to stand there and let me get to the end of the sentence.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: You knew I was pregnant.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: I knew the baby's time was close.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Nine days old. He said it. That child was *nine days old* when he chose to tell me he was alive, and *four years old* now, and in four years — *(Beat.)*— in four years, that is a long time to be

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: somebody's *news*.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Some of that money came from him.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* How much.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: All of it. The groceries, the school thing, the — *(He stops and starts over, because he can hear what he's doing.)*No. Let me do that right. I got a message from a man who said *don't tell her,

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: I'll call when I can.* He never called. I delivered the groceries. I delivered the *school thing*. I have stood on that step approximately two hundred times, and every single time I thought about

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: telling you where the money was from, and every single time I decided that a *secret I was keeping* was less dangerous than a *hole in your life*.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: And I want to say — I know how that sounds.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: It sounds like a man who loved us and lied to us *at the same time*, and that is a thing I did not know could be one sentence, and I have had four years and I still don't have the word for it.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: You shouldn't have to find one tonight.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Who told you not to.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Your father.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: My *father* told you not to tell my brother's partner that my brother is alive.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: He said getting in touch could put them in danger. *(Beat — and he is very careful now.)*And I want to say something about that, because Blue is about to do a thing and I'd rather he did it with

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: the whole shape. He also said, and he said it *first*: he said the danger had passed three years ago.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: Then why didn't you—

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Because then I'd have had to have a *conversation* instead of a *favour*.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: What's on the envelope.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* Nothing.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: It's a *tape* in a machine. You've carried it four years in a supermarket bag with a *receipt* on it. What's written on the bag.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(He turns it over. There is one line on the bag in his own handwriting.)* "Do not lose."

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: You wrote *do not lose* on the outside of a tape you were not supposed to have.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* I did.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Give it to me.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Baby Momma, it's evidence. If anybody ever wants—

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Nobody is going to want anything. That is the *entire* thing that has happened to this family. Give it to me.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(To the room, generally.)* Tomorrow I'm playing six tables. I want that said *now*, in this room, tonight, so that nobody spends the next twelve hours managing me.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: You're going to see him tomorrow.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: His father is *away until tomorrow evening*. Red will call. *(Beat.)* I'll tell him myself.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: You should bring somebody.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I'll bring somebody who doesn't owe either one of you anything.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: That's not a question, by the way. I'm telling you now so you can spend the night deciding whether to be busy.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(At the door, to nobody in particular, putting her coat on.)*Blue. Your father is going to be very calm about this, and when he's calm like that it's because he's already decided what he's going

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: to lose, and it isn't going to be the conversation you want.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Blue
scenes.text: What is it going to be.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* An apology. *(Beat.)* And you should decide *now* whether you're going to be there for it, because there's not going to be a second one.

tips: The middle district locks in round three for both players.
Plan your early placement around the posted closure.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Red Side Gauntlet. Six tables. Clear all six and you host next week's showcase.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Including the food. Which I have already bought in a quantity that people found upsetting.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Including the food.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I'm not taking questions, I'm just *establishing* that it includes the food, because last time a man said "showcase" and there was a *dry cracker* and a *juice box* and I want everybody to be on

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: notice that this is a *different administration*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Walking past with a deck.)* Don't talk to me about food right now.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Ma'am—

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I've been since six in the morning doing a thing I do not want to talk about, and it went well, and I am *not* going to do it again in front of a bracket sheet. *(To the room.)*I'm playing. I

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: signed up like a *person*. I want an afternoon where I am a person and not a *tragedy in a chair*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: And we're all just supposed to act normal.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: You could start by letting somebody finish a sentence.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I have *never*—

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: You do it every forty minutes and you don't hear it because you talk over the top of it. *(Beat.)* Your father did that too. You are *so* his kid it is a *medical* event.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Table one. Middle closes in round three. Let's give the people waiting an actual match.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: First stamp. Cornball's next, then Snitch. Baby Momma's on the last table.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Not looking up.)* I know where I am. I've had a *bracket*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Table two is Cornball. Table three is Snitch, and Snitch —

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: I'm *aware* of what you were going to say.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: I was going to say turn your camera off during the back room.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: I know. And I've turned it off, and I want it *known* that I turned it off, and I want it *in writing*, because that's a *sacrifice*, and I don't do sacrifices without a *paper trail*.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(To the room, flatly.)* Who told you the back room is a thing.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Everybody tells me.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Mm.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Quickly.)* Which — that came out wrong.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: It came out exactly right, and I want you to hear how right it was, because you didn't know there was a back room until *Red said the back room*, and you've been planning for one for a *week*,

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: which means somebody's been *feeding* you.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Red. Table three — is that Snitch, or is that somebody with a phone?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That's Snitch.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Then here's what's going to happen. He's going to play. He plays *fine*. And then when you say "back room," I am going to look at him, and he is going to put the phone in the *chair*, and nobody

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: is going to talk about it. *(Beat.)*Not because it's a rule. Because I'm going to be able to *see* whether he means it, and everybody in this room has been *asking* me to trust somebody for four

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: years, and I am trying out a *new* thing where I watch instead of trusting.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Quietly.)* That's fair.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Sharply.)* It isn't fair, it's *tactical*. Don't get *sentimental* on me, you're not done yet.

tips: Read the flyer for an optional story beat and a Street Pack Ticket.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: Optional detour, champ. Take a flyer and a ticket. Red asked me to get people to the showcase.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Does the flyer mention food.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: It says "food available."

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(To the player, with genuine betrayal.)*"Food *available*." That's the phrase. That's what they *put*. A man in a *barn* with a *cheese* would never write "food available." A man in a *barn* with

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: a *cheese* would write "THERE IS CHEESE." Those are two different *philosophies*.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: What does the flyer actually say.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: It says, and I'm reading it exactly — "Red Side Showcase. All welcome. Come hungry." *(Beat.)*And I *lobbied* for that last line. I said "Red, a hungry crowd is a *bad* crowd," and he said "Alley,

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: a hungry crowd is a *fast* crowd," and I have been thinking about that sentence for eleven days.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: "A hungry crowd is a fast crowd." Is that a *thing*?

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: It's a *thing now*, because I put it on nine hundred flyers.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: You put that on nine hundred flyers?

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: *(To the cooler.)* I put a *lot* of things on a *lot* of flyers. Anyway. The cooler's free. I'm not charging anybody who plays me.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(Already at the cooler.)* He said *free* to a man he doesn't know at an event he wasn't invited to.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: I said that.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Nobody *witness* that. *(He looks at the player.)* *You* witness that.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: I'm witnessing it.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: *(Almost fond.)* Oh, I like this one. They *document*.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(Taking a flyer, reading it upside down, which is a choice.)* *(Beat.)* I got a question about the flyer and it's a real one and it's the same question I've got about *everything* on this block.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: Shoot.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: It says "all welcome." *(Beat.)*Nine hundred flyers, and not one word about what happens when a man shows up who *isn't* on a list, and everybody who reads that flyer is going to assume there's a

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: list. And the *second* there's a list, champ, then there's a *bigger* list, and then somebody's brother's got a *reason* he's not on it.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: There's no list. That's the flyer, and it's a *promise*, and I put it on the *sticker*, and I've been checking for four days that nobody's put a *second* sticker on it.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Nobody's checked.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: Cornball, I have walked past this board *forty-one times* since Thursday and I have *personally* taken down one flyer where a man had written a number on it in *pencil*. *(Beat.)*It was a *low*

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: number. That's the thing that got me. If he'd written a *high* number I'd understand it. A *low* number means he was doing *math*.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: What was the low number.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: Two.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: What's the real number going to be?

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* About thirty.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: So someone wrote "2" on a promise that means thirty.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah. *(Beat.)* He was doing *math*.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: Ticket's yours. *(Beat.)* And that one's not part of the match.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: What is it?

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: It's a *table*. Thirty-one's the cap and Red set the number before he printed anything, and I wrote the thirty-first name in the margin of a *spare* sheet at four in the morning, and if you host

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: it, that's a *seat*, and I don't need it to be you.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: Why me.

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: Because you'll be the one who has to say the number out loud when somebody comes to the door and asks why there's no list. *(Beat.)*And I'd do it, but I'm the man who *wrote* the number, so it

scenes.speaker: Alley Runner
scenes.text: stops being me saying it. It has to be somebody who'll be *upset* about it, and not just a guy with a cooler.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(To the cooler, quietly.)* "Food available."

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: You're still on that?

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(Not joking.)*Champ, "food available" is what a man writes when he can't afford to *promise* food, and there's a *nine hundred* of these on this block tonight, and every one of them's a person

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: saying *come here* in a way that means *and don't ask what's for dinner.*

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: And?

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*And I don't know how to write the line. I been sitting here *forty minutes* trying to write the line and I got a cheese and I got a cooler and I got a *perfect* noun and I cannot write a

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *verb*.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: What's the verb?

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* "There's cheese." *(Beat.)* That's it. That's the whole flyer. "There's cheese. It's nine dollars. It's mine."

tips: Movement effects can change which districts you hold after reveal.
Leave room to respond instead of committing every card to one lane.

starObjectives.description: Move at least one of your cards.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(To anybody walking by, and he is not selling, he is **welcoming**.)* Table two. Welcome to Liquid Gold. Grab a seat, play your match, and sample the business. Sample it. That's free. *(Beat.)*

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: The sample's a *dollar*, but it's free.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It's not free.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's free *adjacent*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: It's a dollar.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Wifey, the dollar is a *gesture*. The dollar is me saying "I see you, I respect your time, here's a dollar for letting me hand you something." Now here's the thing — — nobody's *gonna* buy off a

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: sample if they don't know what's in it. So you gotta taste it, and then you *know* what's in it, and then it's not a dollar, it's a *conversion*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Cornball.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Mm.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: What's the cheese called.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It's got two names. It's got the *brand* name, which is Liquid Gold, and it's got the *artist's* name, which is Terrence.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Terrence.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Terrence. He's the cheesemaker. He's in a barn, he don't got a website, he don't got a *phone plan*, but Cornball — *(he pats the sign)* — Cornball believes in the man.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: So a man called Terrence makes cheese in a barn he won't describe, and you took his name, and you put it on *that*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Genuinely offended.)* I paid him *up front*, Wifey.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: That's a red flag, Cornball, that's not a defense—

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I paid him up front and he said — and this is the part that stays with me — he said, "You got a good eye, young man." *(Beat.)*I got a *good eye*, Wifey. He looked at my cooler and he said I got a

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: good eye.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: It's nine dollars.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's nine dollars.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: For a slice.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's a *wedge*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: That's not a word that means what you think it means.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It's nine dollars for a wedge of an aged, cave-*something*, and I don't say cave because I don't *know* cave, I just know it sounds like something you'd want to charge somebody money for.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Nine dollars.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: You paid forty for a shirt with your own face on it, brother. *Brother.* I got the receipt in my head forever. I looked at that shirt and I went home and I thought about it for a week.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: That's the most upsetting thing anybody's said at this table.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: He brought up the shirt.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I'm at peace with the shirt. Nobody's at peace with the shirt. *(To the player.)* Nine dollars. The thing is nine dollars.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I'll take a slice.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Caught.)* You — just like that?

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You said a dollar for the sample.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I said *free adjacent*—

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You said a dollar.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Already cutting, because he's a professional.)* Yeah. That's — yeah, okay. That's the right read. Thank you. *(To the room, recovering.)* They understood the model.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: They spent a dollar. That is not understanding the model, that is a person buying lunch.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Shuffle up. Everybody's been talking for four minutes and I'm losing table time.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Shuffle *up*. Right. It's a card tournament. We're at a card tournament. *(To the player, low.)* Don't eat it fast. Eat it slow. Then you'll have to come back.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Second stamp. *(He looks at the stamp, then at the cooler.)* Y'all hear that?

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: I hear that.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: That's the *product*. That's a good sign. That's a sign of *life*, in there.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: That's a lid.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: It's a lid *forming*.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: It's formed. It's *on* the cheese. It's *on it* right now. The cheese is *under a lid*, Cornball.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Genuinely fascinated.)* Oh, that's — okay. That's a texture. That's a *crust*. Somebody want to see this?

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Nobody wants to see it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: ...Y'all got nine more of those, that's a *nine-dollar lid*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I'm leaving.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Champ. Go on. Snitch's table's up. I'll handle the organism.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Calling after them, no shame whatsoever.)* Tell everybody Liquid Gold's open! Tell them the *lid* is a feature! Tell them Terrence says hi!

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Terrence is in a barn, Cornball.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Terrence *knows I'm out here.*

starObjectives.description: Move at least one of your cards.

tips: Snitch gets one extra Motion in round three and one in round five.
Save an answer for each boost rather than spending everything early.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Table three. *(Beat.)* I had a whole *thing* set up here.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I know. I watched you build it.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I'm *deconstructing* it.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Why?

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Because certain people have threatened my equipment.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I asked you to stop filming a closed door.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: In a *tone* the equipment found threatening.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Point it at the cards. You have an *actual tournament* in front of you.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Fine. Cards. *(To the player.)* Don't say anything. I know what I look like. I know a man my age taking down his own set up in a *public space* is not a *look* I'm going to *enjoy*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You going to do a bit about it?

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Yeah. But not the kind you want.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I got a *folder*, champ. I want to be clear about that, because I'm gonna do the bit in about four minutes and I don't want the bit to be the *whole* thing. I got a folder with every *clip* of

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: this family since the second of March. I've got the memorial. I've got a *handheld* of Auntie's *cake*, which I shouldn't have. I've got *Blue* at a *funeral* with his hand *shaking*, and that

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: one's got *four million* views and I *put it up* on the *day*, because it was a *good* clip, and it was the *worst* thing I've ever done and it still runs today.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I know it does.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: You *watched* it?

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Four million times, Snitch. I watched it about nine of them and then I stopped and started *reading* it, which is worse, because reading it means I'm *counting*, and there's a *thing* on that

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: video where Blue's doing a *thing* with his face and I've watched it enough that I could *do* the face, and I have never in my life been able to do *Red's* face, and I used to be able to do Red's

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: face.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Not moving, not looking at anybody.)* *(Beat.)* I'd like to say something about that, but I'm not going to, because she'd be right.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Flatter than the room has heard her.)* You would, too.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(To the room, briskly.)*Anyway! In *other* news, which I have been *sitting* on, and which I am *not* sitting on — *(He visibly deletes the sentence in real time.)*Nope. Not doing that. Red,

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: table three, I'm *clean*, I'm *legible*, look at my *face*, I've got nothing *planned*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: You had it loaded.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I had it *in the chamber*, Red. I'm a *professional*, I'm just not a *criminal*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: He gets a boost in three and five. I checked the sheet.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I wrote the sheet.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: You wrote the sheet *badly*, and in *three* he gets a card draw he's not supposed to get, and I want that on the record as me *talking*, because in about an hour I'm going to be in a room and I

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: will not be *talking* about that.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Blue's side gets a boost in two and four. Red's gets one in three, one in five. I wrote them. I wrote them *last* night, and I want to be very clear that I did not do it because of *who* was

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: playing, I did it because Red's been asking me for *two* for two years and I said *no*, and then last night he asked me for *two* and I said *yes*, and that is the *entire* story and I'd like

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: nobody to make it into anything.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Why would you say yes now.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Because last night his father came to this building and told me a thing that I've been keeping since March, and I have been *counting* all night, and I am *tiring* of counting.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Immediately, standing up, phone already coming out.)* Okay, okay — that's *content*, that's a *reaction* —

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Put it away.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(He doesn't. He looks at Baby Momma.)* *(Beat.)* *(He puts it away.)* Yeah. No. Fair.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Third stamp.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: You know what the worst part is? I've been *thinking* about that. I wasn't going to post it. I *decided*, in that match, while I was losing, that I wasn't going to post it. I got there on my

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *own*. In *eight years*, that's never happened once.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: That's because you just watched a man deliberately lose to somebody. Your whole thing is that nobody's ever *beaten* you. *(Beat.)*Snitch, when Red beat you in *round three* just now and you sat

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: down, you did a thing with your face. You went *honest* for about half a second. I saw it. *(Beat.)*That's the first *real* footage you've ever gotten and you *threw* it away, and I want you to

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: think about that on the drive home, because I *think* about it every time I see your channel.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(Very quietly.)* Yeah.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Come with us for a minute. I want someone in that room who doesn't owe either brother a favor.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: So I'm not invited.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: You understood the sentence perfectly.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, and he's trying for a joke and it doesn't come.)* Kid, if I'm not in the room then nothing I do next matters and I *know* that, and I'd like it on the record that I *know* it.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Not invited.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Cool. I'll be outside.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(At the door, not turning around.)*You'll be *at the back*. Not outside, not in the doorway, not behind a thing. *At the back*, facing *away*, and if you turn around before you're told to, I will

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: end this friendship and I don't have a lot of those left.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* ...At the back. Facing away.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Thank you.

tips: Follow the conversation at your own pace.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: Sit wherever there's a plate. *(Beat.)*Yes, I fed you before asking questions. I know this family. I *fed you first* because I know what this family does, which is talk first and eat at nine, and

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: nobody is eating at nine tonight.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: *(Hand up.)* I'm her little brother. I'm here because Red's answers seem to require an audience.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: You're here because I asked you. Don't turn it into a show.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: I'm not turning it into—

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Roaster, you have *been* turning it into a show since you were *nineteen*, and I love you, and if you make a joke in the next ten minutes I'm going to hand you to Auntie and she's *worse* than me.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: She's not worse. I timed it. I'm *not* going to say it, though, because I'm *loyal*, and because she's *right here*, and because—

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Roaster.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: Shutting up.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Not sitting.)* Red. When he told you not to bring that message to me — did you ever ask him if it was still dangerous.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: No.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Once.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Once.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Did you ask him in a *month*. In *three months*. I don't mean the first time. I mean — Red, this could have been *any* time in a *year*, and I want to know if it crossed your mind that there was a

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *week* where you could have said "hey, it might be safe now."

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*No. *(Beat.)*And I want to be honest about why, because if I say "I was protecting you" then I'm doing a thing where I'm *good*, and I'm not. For the first few weeks I believed it. I had

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: a *reason* and I was *using* the reason. And then — *(Beat.)*— and then it stopped being about her and started being about me, because the longer I left it, the *longer* it got, and there was a

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *moment*, and I remember the moment, it was about *five months in*, and I thought: if I tell her now, I have to *explain* five months. So I waited. And then it was *nine* months and I had to

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: explain *nine* months. And then it was a *year*, and I was not a man protecting a woman any more, I was a man who didn't want to have that conversation.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: I had a *reason* for about five weeks and then I had an *excuse* for the rest of it, and I never once told anybody the week it changed.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Serving.)*That's the first true thing anybody's said in this room tonight and it took *eleven months* to get it out. *(Beat.)*Nobody here is going to help you by making it shorter. Say it the

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: long way, baby.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* I let you think I was doing all of it myself.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: *(And he doesn't make a joke.)*You stood at our door holding diapers and that secret. Every time. For four years, there was a man on our step with a bag of *nappies*, and my sister is in there

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: *dying* about it, and every single time you had the *perfect* opportunity to say *one word*.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: I know.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: And every single time you handed them to me, because I was the *funny* one, because I would have *taken* it and made it a *joke*, and it would have been a *great* joke, and it would have been the

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: only *joke anybody made about it*, and you *let* me do that.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Very quietly.)* Roaster.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: You *handed* it too. You came in here and told me you were there because Red's answers needed an audience, and that was *true*, and it was also the *whole* reason you were allowed in the room.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* ...Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Don't be the funny one about this. I can't lose *both* of you in one week.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: The recorder stays with her. All of them — every message, every scrap. He doesn't keep a copy. Nobody on this street keeps a copy. *(Beat.)*She decides what happens to them, when, and to who, and

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: everybody in this room has to be able to live with that, including the ones who think they're being *robbed*.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: That's her call.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: It's *not* her call, it's *yours*, and you just said it, and I heard you. *(Beat.)* Baby. What do you actually want done with it.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I don't want it *done* with. I want to *have* it. *(Beat.)*There's a difference and it's the whole difference. I don't want to release it, I don't want to burn it, I don't want it in a *court*, I

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: don't want it on a *channel*. I want it in a *drawer in my house* that he can't get into, for as long as I want it in there, and I want him to know it's in there *every single day of his life*,

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: and I want him to know I could.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* *(Softly.)* That's a hard thing to hold.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I have been holding a hard thing for four years, Auntie. I'm not putting it down because it's a *nice* afternoon.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: You're the reason I'm talking to you instead of to a lawyer, so say something, because you've been *quiet* and I have a *rule* about quiet.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: You've known all of it. You've been waiting for him to say it on his own, because if he says it, it means you were right to wait.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*Nobody's ever — *(Beat.)*Yeah. *(Beat.)*And you just said it out loud in a *room*, which means I don't have to defend it, and I want to be clear that I noticed you doing that and I'm

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *grateful* and it's *not* going to change how I treat you.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: Wasn't trying to change how you treat me.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Good, because it's *awful* and I like it.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: Can I say one thing.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: If it's a joke—

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: It's *not* a joke. *(Beat.)* It's a *job*.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* Go on.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: *(Clearing.)*I've been putting a *bad* thought in everybody's head since I got here, and I want it out of the room. My bit is that when this is over, somebody's going to be a *hero*, and they're

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: going to be *me*, and it isn't going to be true, and I'd like the *actual* person to know now that they don't *owe me a thing*.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Eventually.)* Plates.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: Yeah.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: Roaster, you're on the same as everybody.

scenes.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* Thank you.

tips: Roaster starts with one extra Motion and favors disruption.
Protect a key district and avoid putting your entire plan on one target.

preDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
preDialogue.text: Table four. I had twenty minutes of jokes prepared about the champion.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: And somehow every single one was about my ex.

preDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
preDialogue.text: There was *crossover appeal*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Put the microphone down.

preDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
preDialogue.text: It's a *napkin*.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*It's a napkin with a *bit* in it and you brought it to a *card table*, and Roaster, I *loved* what you just said in that room, so please don't do this, because you are about to be

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: extremely funny and I am going to have to be the one who says it's not the right time.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Roaster, you just got told by the person who likes you most that she doesn't want you to work right now. That's a *gift*. Most people have to *pay* for that.

preDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(To the player.)* You hear that? She just *bought* me from her. This is a *transfer*. I'm *hers* now.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: You are *not* hers. You are *sitting down*.

preDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
preDialogue.text: Fine. But I want it *noted* that the *bit* was good.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: The bit was *terrible*.

preDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
preDialogue.text: It was *structural*.

preDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
preDialogue.text: *(Dealing, not looking up.)*I'm playing. I'm just going to say — I can't do a bit right now. I can't. I did about four in that room and Auntie took the *plates* away, so I'm running on *nothing*,

preDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
preDialogue.text: and this is the best I can do, and if I go quiet mid-match somebody tell me a *punchline* and I'll take it.

postDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
postDialogue.text: Fourth stamp. *(Beat.)* That was the worst game I've ever played in a *venue* I was *briefed* for.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: You played like a man who was thinking about something else.

postDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah. I been thinking about the *napkin*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: What napkin.

postDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*I had a bit. I really did. It was about a man who runs a *funeral* like a *fundraiser* and it was *great* and I wrote it down and I brought it *here*, and I want you all to know that I

postDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
postDialogue.text: chose not to use it and it *cost* me something, and I don't know what I'm gonna do with myself now that I've decided I'm allowed to be *bored*.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Passing.)* You want these out to the kitchen?

postDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Please.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: The volunteers haven't eaten. *(Beat.)*And Roaster — you're on the same as everybody, so you're *coming*, and you can have the last plate, and that's not a *joke* and I'm not going to *perform*

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: it.

postDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *(Very quiet.)* Okay.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(To the room, cheerfully.)*Kitchen's *served*. And the *thing* at the back — the *room* — the *back* of the back room — — I have *four* chairs and one of them is *Roaster's*, and Roaster's is the

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: one *next to the door*, and I want everybody to know that I put it there *specifically* so he could leave without anybody having to *look* at him.

postDialogue.speaker: All Jokes Roaster
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Cornball.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: I'm a *setup volunteer*, I don't have *opinions*, and I have *furniture*.

tips: Wifey's opponent hand starts at six cards.
Existing protection can block targeted effects; choose your timing carefully.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Table five. Somebody finally took check-in off my hands.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: My wife is dangerous at this game.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: You could have told the room that before asking me to run your errands all morning.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You didn't *hear* me asking.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: I *heard* you asking. I heard you ask four times in a tone like you were *appointing* me, and I said yes to every single one, and there is a *difference* between those two things, and the

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: difference is that the second one had a *price* on it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, cheerfully.)* She codeswitches. Watch. It's the best part of my life.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Somebody came through check-in at a quarter past three who is not on the sheet, and I gave him a number and *not* a sticker, and Blue would like to know why I did that.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Why did you do that?

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Because he's not on the sheet.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I didn't know he wasn't on the sheet.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Then the sheet is wrong, and *that's* why I didn't give him a sticker, and I'm not going to explain it twice on a *Tuesday* when you're about to play cards at a *fundraiser*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, in the other one, warm.)*Anyway! *Hi.* I've been wanting to say — in that room tonight, when you said the thing about people who check their seats, that was the single best

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *observation* made by any human being in the history of this *event*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Thank you.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: You're welcome. You're also the only person who's thanked me in about *four years*, which is a *problem* I'm going to work on separately.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: (to nobody) She's got that too.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Got what?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: The read.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Blue, you play her every week.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I play her every week and I *lose* every week and I *keep* doing it, and I want you to understand that that's a *choice* and it's a *bad* one.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Where'd you get that.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Somebody's second hand.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Somebody's *second hand*. *(Beat.)*I held that for four plays because I needed to know it was the only one. That's not *skill*, that's *accounting*, and Red does that, and I learned it from

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: watching a man do it for four years.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Wifey.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, not to him.)*You're in the back room in twenty minutes and I'm not going in there, and I want you to know that, and I want you to know *why*, and then I'm going to go and *count*

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: something.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: I spent four years being the person who *knows where everything is*. Files, money, rosters, a *tape* in a *bag*. *(Beat.)*And in that room tonight I found out the *tape* had a *second* custodian,

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: and he had it for four years, and he never *told me*, and I have been standing in this building telling people the *records are intact*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: They *are* intact—

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: They're intact because I'm *tall*, Blue. Not because we're *honest*. *(Beat.)*I'm not going in that room because I have got about nine questions and they are all for *me*, and I am not going to

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: stand in a room and ask them *tonight* in front of *him*.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: I'm handing this to the person who doesn't owe anybody a favor. Not today. When you're ready. *(Beat.)*There's a name on the bottom of that page that two men in this family have been *pretending*

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: is a courtesy, and it stopped being a courtesy in about *April*, and I have been *holding* it, and I am *done holding it*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Whose name is on the bottom.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Mine. *(Beat.)* It's my name, and my address, and a call I've been putting off since March, and it is *not a bit*, and I would like everybody in this room to have seen me say that.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Ma'am, I been running a clipboard on this block for *years* and I have *never once* had a person hand me a *thing* like that and I have got *no idea* what to do with a *thing* like that.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: Write it down.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* *Write it down.* *(Beat.)* Right. *(He writes it. He does not joke. He writes it.)*

tips: One extra CPU Motion arrives in round three.
A Wifey card reinforces the CPU side in round five. Plan for its protection.

phases.name: Don't Rush Me
phases.description: At round three, Baby Momma gains one extra Motion once.

phases.name: She Brought Backup
phases.description: At round five, add one Wifey reinforcement to the CPU side once.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Last table. I'm playing for the showcase too, in case everybody forgot that I signed up like a *person*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: *(At the wall. He has been there for an hour and has not sat down.)* I didn't forget you could play.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Great. Then you won't need to narrate it.

preDialogue.speaker: Church Auntie
preDialogue.text: *(Already at the adjacent table with her deck.)* There's a chair by me. You can watch quietly.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Thank you.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: Winner hosts. I want space for the families, and food for the people doing setup, in that order, because that's the order that makes it a *thing* and not a *party*. *(Beat.)*And if I win, that's

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: the list, and I don't want to be asked for anything else. If I lose, the list goes to Red and I *will* have an opinion.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, genuinely quiet.)*She just said "food for the people doing setup." *(Beat.)*That's *me*. She just said the *thing* about me in front of *everybody* and she didn't even *look* at

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: me.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: *(Sitting down heavily.)* I did it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: You did it.

preDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
preDialogue.text: I have not *won* anything since the second of March. *(Beat.)* That's a horrible thing to say out loud at a *card table* and I'm going to say it again later when I can stand up.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Good match.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Beat. Beat. Beat.)* That was the message.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I know.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Four words. That was *four words* and I have had it in a *drawer* for four years.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: I know.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Fine. *(Beat.)* Good match.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Red. Did OG answer.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: He's home. He knows we're coming.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: Your coat's in the car. Get your coat. I'd like you there.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Why me.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Flat, and it's the flattest thing she's said.)*Because in about two hours, in a room with a man in it who has *not* been honest with anybody in four years, there is going to be one other person

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: at that table. And I would like it to be a person who has *heard me say my own numbers today*, and doesn't owe a *thing* to anybody in that room, and who has *not* been *lying* to me about

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *cheese*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Loudly, immediately, and it is the *release*.)* THE CHEESE.

postDialogue.speaker: Baby Momma
postDialogue.text: *(Not turning.)* Cornball, I will *end* you.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: She said the *cheese*, champ. *(Beat.)* In front of the *whole event*. I want a *frame* around that.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(Getting their coat.)* *(To Cornball.)* It's not a frame.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* It's *absolutely* a frame. I'm putting it on a *clipboard*. I've got a *pen*.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(To the player, at the gate, quietly.)* There's no chair for you inside. There's four chairs and it's four people.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: I'll stand.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* No. You'll come in. She asked for you and I've been outvoted.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Red. I wasn't expecting this many people.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Not sitting.)* You were expecting me. Let's start there.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Did you tell him to let me believe Cracked Head was dead.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: That's it? You're not going to—

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: No. *(Beat.)*I've been *waiting* four years for somebody to make me say the next part, because I've written it down about nine hundred times and every version of it makes me look like a man with a

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: *reason*, and I have got about eleven weeks of energy and I'd like to spend them being *accurate* instead of *justified*.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Go on, then.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: *(And he sits down, slowly, which is the whole tell.)*There were men after your man. I'm not going to soften that and I'm not going to make it sound like a *situation*. After the handoff went bad

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: there were people on this block who wanted to know where he was and who he'd *told*, and one of them was a man in a *car*, and he was asking about the *warehouse* on a Tuesday.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: And you told them he was dead.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: I told the *block*. *(Beat.)*I told you first. That's the order and I'm not going to pretend it was the other way round, because if I say I told the block first then I'm a man who protected a

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: *neighborhood*, and I didn't. I told *you* first, and then I told the block, and I did those two things about four hours apart, and in those four hours I could have *stopped*.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Why didn't you stop.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: Because I had a card.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: I want to show you something, because I have been carrying it and I have not shown a *soul*, and my hand is going to be bad at this in about a minute.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: That's not him. It's mine. It came in the post the Tuesday after, to a *wrong* address, because the *worst* thing about that week is that people were still *writing to me about him*, and I'd been

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: getting them for *months*, and I was putting them in a *drawer*.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I know about the letters.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* You *know* about the letters.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Four hundred, Red brought me four hundred. There's a *woman* in Ridgemont who's been writing your son a birthday card since the *second year*. *(Beat.)*I know because I answer them. I answer all

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: of them. I put *my* return address on and I write *he is not able to write* and I *sign* them, and I have signed *four hundred* letters to people about a man who is *alive*, and I'd like somebody

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: here to tell me what that is, because I have been calling it *paperwork* for a *very* long time and I am starting to think it isn't.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* You know what that is.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I want to *hear* it.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*It's a *job*, Baby Momma. *(Beat.)*It's a job you did *badly*, and you did it for four years, and I know that, and I know what it's *cost* you, and I am *not* going to be the man in this

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: porch who says that, because you already know, and because the second I say it I'm the one standing in front of a thing I did, and I *would* do that, and I'd do it right now, and that's exactly

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: why I'm not doing it.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Quietly.)* That's the first time tonight you've talked like a person.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* I'm working on it.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: And did you ever plan to tell me.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: No. *(Beat.)*I kept putting it off. And then there was no decent way to explain *how long* I'd put it off, so I found a worse way, and then there was no way at all, and by then it was a *thing I

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: was doing* rather than a *thing I hadn't done yet*, and that's how it became permanent. *(Beat.)*I want to be very clear that at no point did I decide to lie to you forever. I decided it a week at

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: a time. For two hundred weeks.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Low.)* Blue's not here.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I know.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: He doesn't know yet.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: I know that too.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* Do you want him here?

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*No. *(Beat.)*If he's in this porch right now he will spend the next ten minutes trying to *help me be angry*, and he will do it because he is *good*, and then I will be angry at *him*

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: instead of at the *man in the chair*, and I have been angry at the wrong person for four years and I am *not doing it again tonight*.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: You're the one who's been writing things down.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: I'm the neutral one.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*There is no neutral. *(Beat.)*That's what I want to say to you tonight, and I want to say it before I get tired, because I can hear myself starting to *ramble* and I've got a bit left.

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*There is no *neutral* in this porch. There are four people on a step and you are the only one who doesn't love anybody here, and that's not a *freedom*, that's a *job*, and you're doing

scenes.speaker: OG Uncle
scenes.text: it *tonight*, and if you go home tonight and say "I was just there," then you *weren't*, because a person who was just there does not do what you just did for that woman.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Getting up.)* You should have told me a week at a time. That's the whole thing. If you'd said *one week* to me, in the *first* year, I would have hated you and then I would have had a *year*.
